svg.title: One UUIDv7, six representations — with a masking avalanche example
svg.desc: The same UUIDv7 shown as standard text, 16 bytes, plain base64url, plain base32hex, masked base64url and masked base32hex. Colours connect timestamp, version, variant and payload fields across plain encodings. A table compares use, time ordering and case when decoding. The masking inset flips the last UUID bit with the same demo key and settings: all 16 bytes of the masked block and all 22 base64url characters change in this example. This does not mean all bits flip or establish cryptographic strength.

Counts describe this pair only." }

g.text: Text, bytes & plain slugs: any UUID, no key. Masked slugs: UUIDv7, matching key.
Same bits, different encoding. Unmasked UUIDv7 time stays readable.

g.title: UUID text
g.desc: 0198abcd-1234-7abc-9def-0123456789ab. 36 chars · lowercase. UUID columns & UUID-only APIs. Same-case ASCII. Case-insensitive. Time-range queries on UUIDv7 keys. 0–9 a–f · hyphens.

g.title: UUID bytes
g.desc: 01 98 ab cd 12 34 7a bc 9d ef 01 23 45 67 89 ab. 16 bytes · shown as hex. Binary storage & transport. Generate / decode into your buffer. UUID byte order. Not text. Validation errors leave the buffer unchanged.
g.text: Validation errors leave the buffer unchanged

g.title: Plain base64url
g.desc: AZirzRI0eryd7wEjRWeJqw. 22 chars. Short URLs, logs & JSON. 14 fewer characters than UUID text. Can reverse times. Case-sensitive. Decode with standard base64url tools. A–Z a–z 0–9 -_.

g.title: Plain base32hex
g.desc: 06canj8i6htbp7ff04hkaps9lc. 26 chars · lowercase. Case-insensitive files & text keys. Time-range queries on the ID. Same-case ASCII. Case-insensitive. +4 characters vs plain base64url. 0–9 a–v.
g.title: Base32 alphabet 0–9 a–v; RFC 4648 §7 base32hex. API constant: BASE32HEX.
Masked base64url
g.desc: ap225Qa_y6wN5LQCJgwH0z. 22 chars. Hide UUID fields; keep database UUIDs. Matching key + settings recover the UUID. Decode to sort. Case-sensitive. Keep old keys + settings for old links. A–Z a–z 0–9 -_.
g.text: Hide UUID fields; keep database UUIDs
Matching key + settings recover the UUID
Keep old keys + settings for old links

g.title: Masked base32hex
g.desc: daerdp86nv5qo3f4mg12c307qco. 27 chars · lowercase. Masked IDs for case-insensitive files. Same UUID + key + settings → same slug. Case-insensitive. +5 chars; the codec reads either masked alphabet. 0–9 a–v.

g.title: o = 11000; 2 Masked payload bits, 3 zero bits

g.text: Same UUID + key + settings → same slug
g.title: Base32 alphabet 0–9 a–v; RFC 4648 §7 base32hex. API constant: BASE32HEX.
g.text: +5 chars; the codec reads either masked alphabet

g.title: Masking: avalanche effect
g.desc: The last UUID byte changes from 10101011 to 10101010: one bit flips. With the same key and settings, all 16 bytes of the mixed output block change for this example. Orange squares each represent one changed output byte. 62 of the block’s 128 bits flip; the remaining 66 do not. The four outer check bits are separate and are not drawn as a seventeenth byte. Branches show influence, not actual cipher wiring.

g.aria-label: Before and after the one-bit change
Mask again with the same key and settings
All 16 output bytes differ in this example

g.title: Byte 3: b6 to de; 3 of 8 bits change
Byte 4: e5 to 44; 3 of 8 bits change
Byte 5: 06 to f9; 8 of 8 bits change
Byte 6: bf to 89; 4 of 8 bits change
Byte 7: cb to 16; 6 of 8 bits change
Byte 8: ac to a8; 1 of 8 bits change
Byte 9: 0d to ce; 4 of 8 bits change
Byte 10: e4 to b9; 5 of 8 bits change
Byte 11: b4 to 75; 3 of 8 bits change
Byte 16: d3 to 81; 3 of 8 bits change

g.text: In this example. Not every bit flips.
Plain and masked base64url can look identical. Choose the reader for the format you issued.
Mask examples use a public demo key
¹ Encoded milliseconds, not event order; sort one case/alphabet. ² Nearby times share prefixes; ASCII can reverse adjacent milliseconds.
Compare decoded UUIDs, not spellings. Masking: 16-bit check; wrong keys can return another UUID · time must fit the configured ~139-year range · not strong encryption.
